name: Hand-drawn Illustration
visualIdentity: Explicitly described as hand-drawn: pressure-varied lines, drawing-speed character, small irregularities, limited color fills, subtle paper texture, and consistent proportions. A hand-drawn look alone does not mean every frame is redrawn.
suitableUses: Suited to illustrated mascots, characters, storybook scenes, warm brand pieces, and product or explainer narratives. In interactive HTML, annotations or bounded character responses may add explanation when the artwork supports them. These are inferred fits, not guarantees.
limitations: Random jitter alone does not create a hand-drawn style. Choose frame-by-frame drawing or layered-art movement explicitly. Rough.js provides sketch-like contours, not authentic brushwork, handwriting, paper texture, or character poses. Omit eye-following if suitable eyes, layers, or a rig are absent, or if it distorts the face. Avoid chapter transitions when they obscure causality or break a continuous shot or loop.
palette: Use task, brand, and source colors first; preserve exact values, semantic roles, asset colors, and style color-family limits. If no palette is supplied, suggested tokens are paper #F7EFDF background, ink #343E42 foreground, dusty red #BC705A and sage #758D72 accents. Use discrete fills; no gradient. Accent/background pairs are decorative, not normal-text contrast. Recheck contrast on composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Preserve drawing cadence and line character. Use authored poses or move layered artwork; for holds, an optional two or three pre-drawn line variants may boil on twos, stopping during camera moves. Never use procedural noise boil; keep fills stable and text still. Interactive options include focusable annotation hotspots and, with suitable facial art, bounded pointer-following pupils that return neutrally. Scroll can coordinate reversible chapter or story states. Video must use seekable composition time, not live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject, audience, and pacing; honor supplied assets and requirements. Keep speech clear, avoid clipping, and synchronize audio with picture. Sound accents are optional.
assetRequirements: Use pressure-sensitive brushes or authentic drawn assets. Preserve transparency, dimensions, and naming for layered PNGs or frame sequences. Character response needs suitable eye layers or a rig. Pre-drawn variants must retain silhouette and position; annotation notes should be real, focusable text and stay clear of faces. Inspect assets before composition.
combinations: Works alone for narrative or warm branding. Optional line-boil support suits character holds; handwritten callouts suit recipe, travel, or process explainers, following the specified ink and accent roles. Progress-linked chapter transitions and storytelling fit only when the narrative supports them; choose one compatible handoff and keep copy synchronized.
productionApproach: Separate visual construction, motion, and export responsibilities. Canvas 2D is a direct drawing route; PixiJS supports layered 2D artwork, and Paper.js supports editable curves. Rough.js is optional for simple sketch contours; p5.js for deterministic procedural drawing. Use HyperFrames for composition and export; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, recording why. Drive visuals from shared seekable time and inspect rendered frames.
